democratic.summary: Documents repeatedly seek universal or broadly accessible affordable coverage, strengthening Medicare and Medicaid, widening eligibility, reducing prescription and out-of-pocket costs, and supporting preventive care.
democratic.caveat: Specific mechanisms and populations vary by year; several examples describe records or system problems rather than proposals.

republican.summary: Documents support affordable access through consumer choice, competition, insurers and providers, targeted coverage, primary care, and protection or restructuring of Medicare and Medicaid.
republican.caveat: Approaches vary from program protection to defined contributions; some examples concern adjacent health or Social Security issues.

dsa.summary: Documents advocate universal single-payer or Medicare for All coverage without premiums or cost sharing, regardless of status, alongside public facilities, expanded services, and cost controls.
dsa.caveat: Earlier documents sometimes support interim public options or state routes; a few examples are pandemic guidance or descriptive claims.

democratic_vs_republican.summary: Democratic examples emphasize universal coverage and public-program expansion; Republican examples emphasize consumer choice, provider competition, targeted access, and limiting government intermediation.

democratic_vs_dsa.summary: Both seek broad access, but Democratic examples retain multiple plans and strengthen existing programs, while DSA examples specify one public single-payer program without premiums or copays.

republican_vs_dsa.summary: Republican examples rely on choice, competition, insurers, and purchasing pools; DSA examples replace fragmented insurance with federally administered universal single-payer coverage.
